item.title: Seto Inland Sea Island Cruise: Sailing Between the Islands — Guide
item.description: The Seto Inland Sea, the sheltered water between Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, is one of Japan’s most beautiful landscapes and was its first designated national park. Strewn with hundreds of green, steeply rising islands and famously calm, it has been a highway for a thousand years, and the best way to appreciate it is simply to get on a boat. Options range from local ferries linking island ports for a few hundred yen, to sightseeing cruises from Hiroshima and Onomichi, to overnight luxury cruise ships.

item.title: Tobishima Island: Yamagata's Remote Sea-Bird Sanctuary — Guide
item.description: Tobishima lies 39 km off the Sakata coast in the Sea of Japan — a small, remote island of roughly 250 residents where time moves slowly and the surrounding waters host enormous colonies of black-tailed gulls (umineko) and other sea birds. The ferry from Sakata takes two hours, and the island’s clifftop trails, fishing harbour and near-total absence of tourism make it one of Yamagata’s most rewarding off-the-beaten-path experiences. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Tobishima, off Sakata, Yamagata Hours Ferry ~1–2 sailings/day (seasonal) Admission Ferry ~¥3,000 round trip Time needed Full day Best time Late spring–summer (bird colonies, calm seas) What to See Enormous colonies of black-tailed gulls and sea birds.
